items.prompt: A largest-first coin routine matches 100 test cases. What supports a universal correctness claim for a new coin system?

options.text: Agreement on every amount up to the number of denominations
options.why: A bounded range can miss a larger counterexample; it is not a proof for every permitted amount.

options.text: Ignoring any mismatching examples as outliers
A proof that the routine always terminates on positive coins
options.why: Termination does not establish that the number of coins is minimum.

options.text: A proof under that exact domain, not test count alone
options.why: Tests are useful evidence but do not establish every case.

items.explanation: The algorithm and allowed coin system need a correctness argument. Finite testing helps find mistakes, not replace the universal claim.
